intro: An analogy is a pair of pairs: A : B :: C : D means "A is to B as C is to D". Find the rule that turns A into B, then use the same rule on C.

tips.title: Find the rule in the first pair
tips.body: Ask: how do I get from the first number to the second? Try ×, ÷, +, −, squaring and cubing, one at a time.

tips.title: Check it on the second pair
tips.body: A good rule must work on both pairs. Test each option with your rule; only one should fit.

tips.title: Is the second number much bigger?
tips.body: Think squares, cubes or multiplying: 8 : 256 is 8³ ÷ 2, and 5 : 150 is 5³ + 5².

tips.title: Is it much smaller?
tips.body: Think dividing or square roots: 625 : 7 is √625 = 25, then 2 + 5 = 7.

tips.title: Look inside the digits
tips.body: Some rules use the digits: add them (56 → 5 + 6 = 11), subtract them (41 → 4 − 1 = 3), then square or double.

tips.title: The blank can be anywhere
tips.body: In 32 : 2 :: ? : 3, work backwards: 2⁵ = 32, so the missing number is 3⁵ = 243.
